title: Inspection evidence and restricted client handover
audience: Trainee or new worker on the roof soft washing track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Identify conditions, authorisation limits and evidence requirements relevant to inspection evidence and restricted client handover.
Differentiate worker-observable conditions from determinations reserved to qualified roof, electrical, chemical or environmental specialists.
Demonstrate a proportionate stop-work, referral and documented client communication using a paper-based scenario.

instruction.heading: What the client is actually receiving
instruction.body: At the end of a roof soft-washing job the client receives a document, and that document is often the only thing they keep. It is a record of what was seen, what was done, what was not done, and what remains open. It is not a guarantee that the roof is safe, sound, compliant or clear of asbestos. A restricted handover says so plainly. Commercial roofing businesses tend to rely on a clear inspection report with dated photographs and a short statement of scope, and that practice is a useful model here. The difference is that a soft-washing worker is often not qualified to make the determinations a full roof report would contain, so the handover must stay inside what was observed and authorised, and must name the specialists for everything else.

instruction.heading: Evidence that stands up
instruction.body: Evidence is useful when a reader can check it. Each photograph needs a date, a location label that matches the plan, and the name of the person who took it. Keep the original file, unedited, in the job folder, and use copies for the handover. Each observation should state where it was made, from what position, and whether it was seen directly or reported by someone else. A note that says 'roof is fine' cannot be checked. A note that says 'ridge capping lifted at the north-east end, photograph 7, observed from the footpath on the stated date' can be. Record the source of every statement that did not come from you, such as the owner's account of earlier repairs, and mark it as reported.

instruction.heading: Separating facts, unknowns and determinations
instruction.body: Before writing the handover, sort every item into one of three groups. Facts are things you observed and can describe. Unknowns are things you could not see, or things nobody has assessed. Determinations are conclusions that belong to a specialist: whether the roof is structurally sound, whether a material is fragile, whether a chemical is compliant, whether asbestos is present, and whether electrical equipment is safe. A worker does not reach these conclusions in a handover, even when the answer looks obvious. Instead the handover states that the question was not determined, names the person or the type of specialist who must determine it, and records the step required to get the answer. This sorting is the core of the lesson, and a handover that mixes the groups is not acceptable even if every statement in it is accurate.

instruction.heading: Writing the restricted handover
instruction.body: A restricted handover has a set of plain sections. It states the job, the date, the address and the people involved, and the owner or body corporate that authorised the work. It lists what was done, in the order it was done, and which roof planes, gutters or surfaces were covered. It lists what was not done and why, including any area held for access, asbestos, fragility, electrical hazards or chemical approval. It lists each unresolved item with the person who owns it and the approval still needed. It records what was told to the client and when. It ends with a space for the client's acknowledgement that they received the document and understand the restrictions. Where the business uses an approved sign-off procedure, that procedure governs the form. The handover should be short enough that the client reads all of it, and specific enough that nobody can mistake an open item for a finished one.

instruction.heading: Wording that is safe to use and wording that is not
instruction.body: Good wording names the observation, the date and the limit. For example: 'Observed from the ground on the stated date. No structural assessment has been carried out, and that is a determination for a competent person.' Or: 'Wash not carried out on the rear plane, pending access approval from the body corporate.' Avoid words that imply a result nobody has verified, such as 'safe', 'compliant', 'certified', 'clear', 'asbestos-free', 'structurally sound' and 'fully decontaminated'. These words can make a client rely on a safety or compliance position that the worker is not able to give. If a client asks for one of these statements, the answer is that the question is outside the job, and the question is referred to the competent person, recorded, and answered in writing.

instruction.heading: When evidence is missing
instruction.body: A handover does not become complete because the work is finished. If an approval has not been received, a plane is held, an asbestos question is open, or a photograph is missing, the handover must say so. Do not fill a gap with an assumption. If a client asks for a clean certificate while items remain open, decline to issue one, record the request, and state the open items in the handover. If an approval arrives later, issue a dated change note that records the new information and what it changes. Do not re-issue an earlier version of the handover as though it had always said the new thing.

instruction.heading: Damage claims, prior damage and what the record can show
instruction.body: Clients sometimes report damage after a job and ask whether the job caused it. The record is the first and most useful answer. Before-work photographs that show the same tile or sheet with the same crack are evidence that the damage pre-dated the job. Where the before photographs do not show the area, say so. Do not admit or deny cause in a handover or a message. Record the complaint, the date, the photographs compared, and the person who will answer. Keep the originals, and pass the question to the decision owner. The record should show what was seen, not who was at fault.

instruction.heading: Handing over and keeping the record
instruction.body: Give the handover to the client, the owner or body corporate that authorised the work, and the decision owner in the business, and record the date, the method of delivery and the acknowledgement received. Keep the signed or acknowledged copy, the photograph index, the observation record, the hold and stop-work logs and any change notes together in the job folder. Customer personal details in the handover are handled under the business's privacy policy, and the policy is not described here.

procedure: Gather the photograph set and the observation record for the job, and check that each photograph has a date and a location label.
Sort each item into fact, unknown or determination, and move any determination to the list of questions for a specialist.
Remove any statement that implies safety, compliance, structural soundness, asbestos clearance or decontamination.
List what was done and in what order, and list what was not done, with the reason for each item.
List each unresolved item with its owner and the approval still needed.
Draft the restricted handover using the business's approved sign-off procedure, and check that it agrees with the hold and stop-work records.
Give the handover to the client and the decision owner, and record the date, the method and the acknowledgement.
If an approval or new information arrives later, issue a dated change note, and do not re-issue the earlier version as if it had always said the new thing.

workedExamples.situation: A mock job has been completed on the front planes of a roof. The rear plane is on hold, awaiting access approval. The skylights were covered and checked by the competent person on the day. The client asks for a certificate saying the roof is safe and fully cleaned.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What handover is issued, and what is said to the client?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not issue a clean certificate. Issue a restricted handover that lists the front planes as done with dates and photographs, lists the rear plane as held with the approval still needed and the owner of that approval, and records the skylight covers as checked by the named competent person. State that no structural or fragility determination has been made by a worker. Explain to the client, and record in writing, that the certificate was declined because of the open items, and tell the decision owner.

workedExamples.situation: After a wash, the client sends a photograph of a cracked tile and says the job caused it. The crew's after-work photograph shows the same tile, and the before-work photograph of that plane also shows the crack.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is recorded, and what is said?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the client's complaint with the date, then compare the two sets of photographs. The before-work photograph shows the crack, so record that the crack was seen before work. Do not state a cause, and do not admit or deny responsibility. Tell the client that the complaint has been recorded, the photographs have been compared, and the decision owner will reply. Keep the originals and send the file to the decision owner.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks whether the roof is free of asbestos. During the ground walk you saw older fibre-cement sheets on a shed roof, and you did not disturb them.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What wording goes in the handover?
workedExamples.reasoning: Write that the sheets were observed from the ground and were not disturbed, that asbestos has not been assessed, and that an asbestos assessment by a competent person is needed before anything is disturbed. Do not describe the sheets as modern, probably safe or asbestos-free. Record the request, the answer and the referral.

equipmentAndPpe: A camera or phone with date and time stamping on, and a location label for each photograph.
The job pack, the observation record and the approved handover template or sign-off form.
A hold and stop-work log, and a change-note template.
A secure job folder, electronic or paper, for the original files and the acknowledged copies.
PPE is not used for the office part of this lesson. The PPE recorded for any site visit should be listed in the job record.

commonErrors.error: Writing 'the roof is safe' or 'the roof is compliant' in a handover.
commonErrors.prevention: State only what was observed, on what date and from where. Name the specialist who must make any determination.

commonErrors.error: Keeping photographs without a date or location, or editing the originals.
commonErrors.prevention: Date and label each photograph at the time it is taken, and keep the originals unedited.

commonErrors.error: Omitting an open item from the handover because the job looks finished.
commonErrors.prevention: List every hold, unknown and missing approval, with its owner, before the handover is issued.

commonErrors.error: Inferring that a roof is asbestos-free from its appearance.
commonErrors.prevention: Record that asbestos has not been assessed, and refer fibre-cement sheets for a competent assessment.

commonErrors.error: Issuing a second version without a dated change note.
commonErrors.prevention: Issue a dated change note that states what changed and why, and keep the earlier version on file.

commonErrors.error: Accepting a verbal request for a clean certificate.
commonErrors.prevention: Decline in writing, record the request and the open items, and refer the question to the decision owner.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and authority notice: A restricted handover is not a certificate, a licence, a compliance clearance or an authority to carry out regulated work. This lesson does not grant any of these. Refer each determination to the competent person or licensed specialist named in the handover.

Roof risk records: The SafeWork NSW code of practice for work on roofs (cover dated May 2026, commenced 22 May 2026) asks that the risk assessment identify brittle or fragile surfaces, skylights, penetrations and other openings before work begins. A handover that covers a roof in NSW should show that those items were identified and how they were protected. The code does not apply to residential roofs.

Overhead lines in the record: The SafeWork NSW code on work near overhead and underground electric lines (May 2026) says to assume a line is live unless there is an access authority or written documentation from the supply authority. A handover should record that assumption and any referral to the supply authority, and must not record a measured height.

Chemical records: Safe Work Australia's guidance says a hazardous chemicals register lists the hazardous chemicals used at a workplace, with the current SDS for each. A handover that names a chemical should be consistent with the register and with the approval status of that product.

Asbestos in the record: Asbestos removal licence rules are set state by state, and the state-by-state summary is in the asbestos lesson of this course; check the state regulator's page before relying on it. The Safe Work Australia asbestos handling guide (December 2024) does not cover roof sheeting. A handover must not state that asbestos is absent unless a competent assessment says so.

Stop-work rule: Stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the record shows an open hazard, an unapproved product or an unprotected opening, or if a client asks for a statement the worker cannot support. The handover is then issued with the open item recorded, and not held back.

qualityStandard: Every item in the handover is labelled as a fact, an unknown or a referred determination, and no determination is made by the worker.
The handover contains no statement of safety, compliance, structural soundness, asbestos clearance or decontamination.
The handover lists what was done, what was not done with the reason for each, and every open item with its owner and the approval still needed.
Every photograph is dated, located, labelled and kept as an unedited original.
The date, the method of delivery and the client's acknowledgement are recorded, and any later change is issued as a dated change note.
documentationEvidence: A dated photograph index with each photograph's location label, the photographer and the original file reference.
An observation record separating facts, unknowns and referred determinations, with the source of any reported statement.
A restricted handover that states the scope done, the scope not done, the open items, the owners and the acknowledgement.
The hold and stop-work log, and any change notes issued after the handover.
A communication log recording any client request, complaint or refusal, and the answer given.
summary: A restricted handover records what was seen, done, not done and still open. It is not a guarantee of safety or compliance.
Sort every item into fact, unknown or referred determination, and do not make determinations in the handover.
Decline a clean certificate while items remain open, record the request, and issue a dated change note when new information arrives.
Keep the original photographs, the acknowledged copy and the logs together, and refer every determination to the named specialist.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks you to confirm that the roof is structurally safe after you observed it from the ground. Which answer fits this lesson?
options: Yes, the roof is safe, because I was on site and walked across it at the time of the wash and the roof looked fine to me on the day, with no faults seen at all
I observed the roof from the ground on the stated date. No structural assessment has been carried out, and that is a determination for a competent person.
The roof is safe for foot traffic only, which I can confirm from the ground and from my visit on the day, since I looked at it closely
I will confirm it verbally and hold back the written record until the owner asks for it again in the future, once the final payment has cleared in full

knowledgeChecks.question: Which photograph record is most useful as evidence?
options: A photograph with no date, taken on default settings from the path at the front
A photograph edited to remove background clutter before filing it with the job sheet
A dated, located and labelled photograph, with the original file kept unedited.
A photograph sent to the client and not filed with the job record at all today

knowledgeChecks.question: An after-work photograph shows a cracked tile that also appears in the before-work photograph. What should be recorded?
options: The wash caused the crack in the tile, as the photographs show, since the roof was clean before and the tile has changed since
Nothing, because the crack was already there before the work began on the roof and so it is not relevant to the record
Both photographs, with the crack labelled as seen before work, and no conclusion about cause beyond the evidence.
Only the after-work photograph, to keep the file short and easy to read for the client and the owner

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks whether the roof is asbestos-free. You saw fibre-cement sheets but did not disturb them. What is the correct wording?
options: Yes, the sheets look modern and newly fitted to the roof, so they are safe to ignore for the purpose of the wash and the client's question
Probably not asbestos, based on the colour of the sheets and their age and the look of the roof on the day
Asbestos-free for the purposes of the wash, since the wash does not disturb the sheets at all and the roof is fine
Not assessed. An asbestos assessment is needed before anything is disturbed, and that is a competent person's decision.
